answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network enforces quadratic cryptographic stake burning for identity registration. Minting each consecutive identity requires burning tokens at a superlinear cost scaling as O(n^2), creating insurmountable economic friction for attackers. A lone agent at an ivory tower terminal cannot forge swarm consensus across the valley; deploying dummy nodes over the grassy knoll or spoofing verified lotus cluster roots rapidly drains capital exponentially.
